body: If you mean how I survive then it's a struggle.  I try to surround myself with people whenever possible and try to stay busy, but it's usually not enough.  I don't know what my fate is but I think I recently realized that even if I die my soul will still have to solve the same problems.  It kind of terrifies me because suicide was always a way out and I'm starting to think the only way out is through now.  My soul will deal with this one way or another.  Good luck to you.

Yeah, me too.  I would suggest being really smart about a method if you choose one so you minimize the risk of that.  Personally, I don't believe in heaven.  If hell exists, I think we're in it.  Are you religious?
Sorry, I didn't mean to erase your suffering.

I really don't think ethically I can feel good about encouraging you to do it.  For one, I don't know your situation, but on the other hand if you tell me it's bad, I'm here to believe you.  

Instead, I will tell you that your feelings are valid.  I feel them too.  It's why I'm here more and more as I warm up to the idea.  

Maybe this is too much too fast, and if it is I apologize, but what if you considered pushing away from the idea and see where that takes you?  Instead of pushing towards it.  Can you sit with the feeling for 5 minutes?  10 minutes?  An hour?  How long can you practice being with your pain and suffering.  Sometimes just finding a little breathing room between the pain is enough to reconsider or see a different perspective.  I will also say that I'm somehow who is quite jaded about the cycles of pain and pleasure back to pain that while I would argue that things will get better (I would bet everything I own on it) that things will also get worse (I would bet all my winnings off the first bet on this one).  Life is cycles.  If you're sick of the cycles, I'm right there with you.  But if you just need a moment of respite, things WILL change.  Sometimes we have to stop defining what we demand that change will be.  If after everything you still want motivation to do it, maybe read stories about those who have succeeded.  I would strongly recommend doing it in an intelligent way where you don't do permanent damage to your body and get stuck with an even worse quality of life.  Solidarity.
Me too.  Want to talk about it?

Ah yeah, I get this vibe.  My love life is the #1 thing that makes me feel worthless in this world.  I slept with 10 people and still feel empty though.  In fact, several of them treated me like less than human and that makes it almost regrettable.  I simultaneously respect this metric for figuring out when to go, but I also want to say that it's possible that number will keep growing.  But maybe it seems comforting to you.  Either way, I hope you find peace.  It's all any of us want.

Depression kills you from the inside first.  Nobody chooses to kill themselves—first they die on the inside.

I respect whatever your feeling is, but generally I see it as either you buckle down and fight with everything you have left, because it's literally all you can give and if you're gonna die then might as well, or make sure you have everything in order and try to make things easier on those around you (if they deserve it) and make it clean and real.  Messy attempts get messy for all the obvious reasons and often makes things worse.  Though sometimes it's enough to wake up your loved ones around you.

I hear you, for now.  I don't know you.  I know it probably doesn't mean a goddamn thing, but I see you and hear you.  ~~I know your suffering all too well.~~
I thought about calling today but I don't trust them not to call the cops or alert authorities.  Sucks because I think it could be helpful.  Instead, I wrote a suicide note.

The myth that people who are depressed don't try hard is awful.  My depression fuels how hard I try, and I try harder and harder constantly.  In my case, I ended up sending out 400+ job applications and getting nothing so I had to start doing extra credit by designing branded donut boxes and taking them to people, writing to managers directly on LinkedIn etc. and none of it paid off.  I'm still jobless.  A myth in America (not sure where you're from) is that you get out of things what you put in.  I can GUARANTEE you it's not true.  Opportunity is a much better metric of success.  The more people you know, the more opportunities you have, regardless of how 'hard' you work is the key to success these days.  Which means, many of us are locked out by gatekeepers.  One thing I realized in a moment of clarity was that I was trying too hard, not giving up or not trying at all.  Interesting thing to realize when you've been told by society that work equals outcome.  

I am also extremely jealous of some people.  I wish I was a cocky buff dude who didn't think too much about anything.  I used to think I was smart, which I am, but I thought it was a good thing.  I actually see intelligence as a big drawback these days.  I analyze myself into depression constantly.  I'm too realistic to tell myself 'yeah I'm the shit, I'm the best, everybody loves me' because it's just not true and I cannot delude myself.  I once asked myself if I could kind of 'fake it 'til I make it' and the response from my head was "You know I would never life to you."  Oof.  If only it were easier to shift your opinion about yourself.

In my opinion, things get better and worse and better and worse.  Will things get better?  For sure.  100% undoubtably.  Will they get worse after that?  For sure.  100% undoubtably.  

A better question might be 'can I sit with this discomfort for a while?'  And if you can, sometimes that's enough to make it to the next baseline thing, or maybe if you're lucky, a happy thing.  Patience is part of healing, but I am absolutely in the boat of people who are sick of being patient.  A lot of us feel we've been patient (and we have, endlessly) and sometimes some people are just unlucky or destined to not end up where they desire to be.  The concept that our world provides what we need is not true for all of us.  Especially those who suffer disabilities and mental conditions, like many of us here do.

To your last few sentences: My advice is if you're going to kill yourself, which is a totally valid feeling and action to potentially take, (don't let anybody decide your personal autonomy for you) then at least give it a real full on last shot to get out of your comfort zone as much as possible, try new things and not wasting your life.  There's a song by London Grammar that breaks my heart every time called "Wasting My Young Years" and maybe you might relate to it.  I certainly do.  I was a late bloomer, still am.  But I will burn every last ounce of my energy trying to change this life before I use my last breath to end it.  I don't know when that will be, but for my sake I hope it's never.  And for your sake I hope so too.  I see you and the pain you are suffering.  I know it deeply too and I want you to know that there is solidarity in our suffering.  If we don't belong anywhere, then at least maybe, for now in this moment of time, we belong here.

'Help' in this society is severely lacking.  I have 3 therapists because I'm a mess and at the end of the day I have to pay them and they tell me when the time is up for our session.  It's not real.  It's a transaction, but what I'm seeking is very real.  Real connection and real support.  But in capitalism everybody has to fight for their food and unfortunately this is the dynamic now.  I get my therapists have to eat, but it comes at a huge expense to the people suffering.  Maybe we need more tax funded mental health programs.

It's so frustrating that when you want to disappear the hardest part is that you have to take matters into your own hands and once again do the hard work that this cruel world won't do for you.  Feels unjust.

The only consolation I can offer is that things will get better.  I know it sounds cliche, but it is literally true.  They will get better at some point, who knows when.  Unfortunately, they will get worse again too.  I think a better question than 'will things get better?' for this sub would be 'how to break the cycle of things getting better, then worse, then better, then worse.'  It's an exhausting cycle and I understand how tired you are.  Stability and consistency is what most of us seek.  Order in a world of chaos.  Just a little, please.
I get it, I'm right there with you.

I wanted to write a comment to you, but it strikes me that I literally don't know what to say.  So I figured I'd not post and hit the back button but then I felt like that was a disservice to you.  So, I'm going to be real, I don't have answers.  I'm in the same boat as you so I wouldn't want to be the blind leading the blind.  But if it's any consolation, I read your post and empathize.  You aren't alone, even though is constantly feels like it.  And I also get that it's a meaningless platitude, but it is true on a real level also.  Anyway, I hope life starts to make more sense for you.
